claims.explanation: The drug's annotated target HRH2 is unlikely to explain cancer selectivity, and the pattern of sensitive lines is dominated by TP53-mutant, squamous/upper-aerodigestive and KRAS/PTEN-pathway-altered carcinomas, suggesting that ICI-162846 kills cells with defective p53/apoptotic signaling and active RTK/PI3K-MAPK growth signaling. The virtual-cell response (BCL2 up, BAD down, GNAS down, STAT5B/LYN/IKBKE up) points to modulation of survival and inflammatory signaling rather than canonical histamine biology. The most predictive features are therefore TP53 loss-of-function and activating KRAS/BRAF/PIK3CA/PTEN alterations, with squamous lineage as an additional sensitizing context.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is present in nearly all strongly killed lines and absent in several resistant lines; loss of p53-mediated apoptosis is a plausible sensitizer to a survival-pathway-directed drug
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and colorectal lines (T3M4, SNU410, CL11) are among the most killed, consistent with dependence on MAPK/PI3K survival signaling
PTEN loss appears in multiple sensitive lines (786O, TE4, BT549, KALS1) and is absent from most resistant lines, implicating PI3K-AKT dependence
BRAF-mutant CAL12T and K029AX are killed while BRAF-mutant WM793 and SH4 are resistant, suggesting MAPK-driven context contributes but is not sufficient
NF1 loss in BICR6, KALS1 and NCIH2052 may reinforce RAS-MAPK activation in sensitive lines
CDKN2A loss co-occurs with TP53 mutation in many sensitive squamous and NSCLC lines, consistent with disabled cell-cycle checkpoints
PIK3CA mutation is enriched in resistant lines (HGC27, KYSE510, HCC1954, GP2D, SNUC5), suggesting intact PI3K signaling may buffer drug-induced stress
ARID1A mutation appears in several resistant lines (MDAMB175VII, SW1088, HEC265, GP2D, MHHNB11) and may mark chromatin states that evade the drug
STK11 loss in TE4 and KALS1 is associated with sensitivity, possibly through metabolic or AMPK-related vulnerability
SF3B1 mutation recurs in sensitive lines (TE4, UO31, HCC95, CAL12T), suggesting splicing-factor dependency
The annotated target HRH2 is not supported by the killing pattern; high HRH2 expression in resistant lines could buffer any antagonist effect
Virtual-cell response shows BCL2 upregulation, and high baseline BCL2 expression would be expected to protect against apoptosis-inducing stress
